title: More than Circles
subtitle: A ring that closes on itself? That is far from enough to define the essence of "fate."

trails.title: Ushuaia, the End of the World
trails.description: Where is this place? The furthest edge of civilization.

content.text: A gambling game's been set up in a place unfamiliar to you. Soon, you'll be invited to join the table as well.

branch.text: Hmph ... you seem to have grown quite assertive. But remember this: as a newcomer to the table, you have no privilege to make demands or probe for information unless you're looking to be targeted and isolated.

You have to lose a few rounds—pay your "entry fee." Only then can you start to learn the secrets of those at the table. The players' backgrounds, the dealer's habits, and the truth behind the highest-stakes gambler.
It's baffling to me. Why would anyone travel halfway across the world just to throw away their money?
That was a rhetorical question. But thanks for answering.
You're right; the allure of winning is irresistible, even in a game of chance. People blow on the dice, clutch a rabbit's foot, or murmur a prayer, foolishly believing they can sway the outcome.
Tsk, disappointing indeed. To think you're entangled in such empty words.
Some are so captivated by these grandiose phrases that they feel empowered when using them. Despite their vapidity, it makes them feel important.

Oh, quite the opposite. The odds are rarely equal. Your opponents could have any number of advantages stuffed up their sleeves—a larger stack of chips, easier winning conditions, or even the power to change the rules. Want a fair game? You've got to fight for it, by any means necessary.
The white suits always play it safe, carefully hedging their bets, while the black robes plot to overturn the table.
Clever? More like cretinous and atrocious.
Once the table's flipped, there'll be nothing but chaos. Who would bother to set it right again? No one.

items.text: More than Circles

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: According to these news reports from Ushuaia, there was an arcane attack on the pier about a week ago. All the ships in the port were destroyed.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Could Manus Vindictae be responsible for this, or perhaps the Zeno rebels?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hard to say. But things have been suspiciously quiet these past few days.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I had been hoping we'd find some clues here in Ushuaia after we lost track of the Manus in the "Free Breeze" shipwreck.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They would've gone to ground, somewhere remote and off the radar. Indeed, it's possible they've already left Ushuaia.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: For whatever reason, it seems they haven't been pushing for the "Storm" to happen quite as eagerly as before.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I have a strange feeling about it all. They're definitely up to something.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: For now, it seems our new friend's story lines up with the intel from Moth. It seems the Zeno rebels really did bring Dr. Dores here. We should see if there's anything more she can tell us.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper ...
The chief assistant hesitates.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The Foundation doesn't have any intelligence on Tierra del Fuego. If the Manus really are here ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Then, we'll be on our own. The closest Foundation Branch is in Buenos Aires, 3200 km away.
She reflects without words, a reminder that the chaos caused by Igor's rebellion is still fresh.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Careful and well-considered as ever, Sonetto. It's possible they've already infiltrated Ushuaia, just as they did in Chisos.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But the Zeno rebels may still be holding Dores. We can't just wait around. I'm afraid we'll have to take the risk.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ushuaia's not very big. If Manus Vindictae is here, we'll notice. Stay sharp.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Understood, Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'll keep an eye out for them and for Dr. Dores.
After a chaotic "hunt and escape," the café regains its usual peace.
The gendarmes are gone, and so too are Recoleta's companions.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: My friends ... They're really gone.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: "Goodbye, Recoleta. I don't think we'll meet again—" So that's all I get?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: We could've exchanged some farewell poems, read them out loud like we used to, and shed a few bitter tears over our heartfelt goodbyes.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: But you know what they say: "Goodbyes are only a senseless feast of unhappiness."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Pardon?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Oh, it's nothing. Never mind. Please, sit down. And could we get a pot of mate with mint, please?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Thank you.
Recoleta watches with interest as the two girls take the offered cups of tea.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: So, you're looking for Dores?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I can tell she's important to you from your look.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Correct. Is there anything more you could tell us about the day you met her?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Of course. It was one of those gray, overcast afternoons ...

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I had just turned onto Calle Bolivar when I ran into this blind woman on my way to the post office.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: To be exact, I didn't run into her. She called to me. It felt like a sacred moment in time, like something unworldly. I just stood there, frozen, as she walked up and fixed a loose thread on my sweater.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I stared at her until my fingers went numb and the letter almost slipped out of my hand.

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: Miss, could you tell me what's in that direction?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I followed her hand as she pointed forward. Strangely, even though I could see she was blind, I had a feeling that she knew exactly where she was pointing and where she intended to go.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: That's the way to Comala Prison, madam.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Is that where you're headed? I could walk you there, if you'd like.

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: Thank you, Miss. But I think I've found my way.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: She held a typewriter. How ironic that God would give her at once both books and night.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I'm Recoleta. What may I call you, Ms. ...?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I hope you don't mind me asking, madam. I didn't mean to pry.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: It's only that I have to know. You're a writer too, aren't you? I've been working on a novel, and for some reason, I have this feeling you could be a character in it!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Forgive me. I'm just so excited! I really want to remember this moment. Please, may I have your name? Or whatever you'd like me to call you?

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: Heh heh.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I don't think I'll ever forget her smile. It was soft, kind, almost merciful, and oddly, it felt so ancient.

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: No offense taken, Ms. Recoleta. But first, I have a question for you.

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: What does literature mean to you?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Sorry?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: What a question it was! I wasn't expecting anything like it!

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: You're a writer, are you not? And one, I sense, with purpose. Tell me—where does such powerful motivation come from?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Actually, well, I'm not sure, madam.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I have my pursuits and questions, but literature is neither the goal nor the answer to them. Literature is ... Well, it's just literature.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I suppose if I had to define it, I'd say it's a tool, a kindling for fire, or a lens to see through, a means to explore and raise questions from different angles and express our perspectives.

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: And what an interesting perspective you've expressed. I see.

items.speaker: Dores
items.text: But how does literature make you feel?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: As though I'm a kid looking through a kaleidoscope for the first time.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Well, maybe that's not the best way to put it. Perhaps something a little more subtle.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Just when I was looking for the right word, she turned away with a little wave, heading toward the prison, her feet crunching over the fine snow.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: So, she must've gone to the prison!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: When did all of this happen?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: About three days ago. I remember the sun came out for a while that day, and the streets were glistening with melting snow.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: You've heard of Comala Prison, haven't you?
Word by word, the question turns from an implication into a declaration.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Three days ago? Then we may be able to catch up with her there, Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You're right. We need to get there as soon as we can.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Whoa. Amazing! So decisive, assertive—a true show of character!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: You must be the very archetype of a charismatic leader!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: What's left to say? Whenever the protagonist has what they want fall into their laps, we're all quick to complain about lazy writers using "deus ex machina" to keep the story together. So let's not dwell on it.
She reconciles this observation with a silent nod to an unseen author.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: But anything can happen in a place like Ushuaia. It's a city where the day may only last four hours and the streets are full of exiled arcanists.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We appreciate your help, Ms. ...

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Recoleta. Please, think nothing of it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Recoleta, I'm Vertin, and this is Sonetto. We're investigators from the St. Pavlov Foundation.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Pleasure to meet you.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Likewise, likewise! Glad that I could help. But listen, ladies.
The girl winks playfully.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Everything happens for a reason, and now it's becoming clear. You're going to Comala Prison, and so am I.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Maybe it's fate that brought us together.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What's your business there, if you don't mind our asking?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Oh, it's a ... writer's mission. But anyway, we're friends now.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: If you're going to Comala, you'll need someone who knows the way.
